title: Network Interface Errors
exclusions: Detects increases in the aggregate Linux receive-error, transmit-error, and collision counters exposed by the `interfaces` source type. It does not count dropped packets, calculate an error percentage, identify a cable/NIC/driver root cause, monitor switch-side counters, or prove service impact or regulatory compliance. The catalogue SPL applies no maintenance or interface exclusions by default.
evidence: When deployed, retain the `linux_interface_error_increase_5m` saved-search definition, scheduler and alert history, and dashboard exports showing `_time`, `host`, `interface`, the three counter deltas, `new_interface_faults`, and `counter_reset`. These artifacts demonstrate search operation and observed counter changes; they do not demonstrate root cause or regulatory compliance.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a temporary test index with the `interfaces` field extractions, create samples for `host=linux-test`, `Name=eth0` in adjacent complete five-minute buckets: first `RXerrors=100`, `TXerrors=7`, `Collisions=0`, then `RXerrors=103`, `TXerrors=7`, `Collisions=0`. Run the SPL with bounds covering those two buckets and the temporary index. Expect exactly one latest-bucket row with `rx_error_delta=3`, `tx_error_delta=0`, `collision_delta=0`, `new_interface_faults=3`, and `counter_reset=0`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Create adjacent-bucket samples for `host=linux-test`, `Name=eth1` with unchanged values `RXerrors=20`, `TXerrors=4`, `Collisions=0`, and for `Name=eth2` with a reset from `RXerrors=80` to `RXerrors=2` while the other counters remain zero. Run the same bounded test. Expect no result for either interface: unchanged counters have zero deltas, and a decrease is a reset/discontinuity rather than 78 new errors.

dataSources: `index=os sourcetype=interfaces` events collected on each Linux host by the `interfaces.sh` scripted input in the Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833). The add-on supplies search-time fields `Name`, `RXerrors`, `TXerrors`, and `Collisions`; `host` and `_time` are Splunk metadata. `os` is a local index choice, not a vendor-required name.
app: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833), installed on Linux Universal Forwarders for collection and on the search tier for its search-time knowledge objects.
spl:
index=os sourcetype=interfaces host=* earliest=-15m@m latest=@m
| eval interface=Name, rx_errors=tonumber(trim(RXerrors)), tx_errors=tonumber(trim(TXerrors)), collisions=tonumber(trim(Collisions))
| where isnotnull(interface) AND (isnotnull(rx_errors) OR isnotnull(tx_errors) OR isnotnull(collisions))
| bin _time span=5m
| stats latest(rx_errors) as rx_errors latest(tx_errors) as tx_errors latest(collisions) as collisions by _time host interface
| where _time+300<=now()
| sort 0 host interface _time
| streamstats current=f window=1 last(rx_errors) as previous_rx_errors last(tx_errors) as previous_tx_errors last(collisions) as previous_collisions by host interface
| eventstats max(_time) as latest_bucket
| eval rx_error_delta=if(isnotnull(previous_rx_errors) AND rx_errors>=previous_rx_errors,rx_errors-previous_rx_errors,null()), tx_error_delta=if(isnotnull(previous_tx_errors) AND tx_errors>=previous_tx_errors,tx_errors-previous_tx_errors,null()), collision_delta=if(isnotnull(previous_collisions) AND collisions>=previous_collisions,collisions-previous_collisions,null())
| eval counter_reset=if((isnotnull(previous_rx_errors) AND rx_errors<previous_rx_errors) OR (isnotnull(previous_tx_errors) AND tx_errors<previous_tx_errors) OR (isnotnull(previous_collisions) AND collisions<previous_collisions),1,0)
| eval new_interface_faults=coalesce(rx_error_delta,0)+coalesce(tx_error_delta,0)+coalesce(collision_delta,0)
| where _time=latest_bucket AND new_interface_faults>=1
| table _time host interface rx_errors tx_errors collisions rx_error_delta tx_error_delta collision_delta new_interface_faults counter_reset
| sort 0 -new_interface_faults host interface
description: Reports one row per Linux host and network interface when receive errors, transmit errors, or collisions increase by at least one count in the latest complete five-minute bucket. It compares cumulative counters with the preceding bucket, rejects decreases as resets, and reports both current counter values and newly observed increments.
value: Fresh interface faults can reveal a failing adapter, physical-link problem, driver regression, or duplex issue before intermittent packet loss becomes an application outage. Alerting on new increments instead of nonzero lifetime totals prevents the same historical error from paging operators every five minutes.
implementation: Deploy Splunkbase app 833, enable its existing `interfaces.sh` event input at a 60-second interval into the locally selected operating-system index, and verify `Name`, `RXerrors`, `TXerrors`, and `Collisions`. Schedule the search every five minutes over its embedded 15-minute lookback; begin with one new fault count per five-minute bucket and tune by interface class.
visualization: Use a latest-results table with host, interface, each five-minute delta, total new faults, and reset flag. Add separate timecharts for `rx_error_delta`, `tx_error_delta`, and `collision_delta`; label the y-axis as counter increments per five minutes, not an error rate or percentage.
dataModelAcceleration: The add-on documents `sourcetype=interfaces` as Inventory data, but the Inventory.Network dataset normalizes interface identity rather than `RXerrors`, `TXerrors`, or `Collisions`. There is therefore no equivalent CIM `tstats` search for this detection; use the raw source-type fields and do not present Performance.Network throughput as an error-counter substitute.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Planned NIC, driver, or virtual-interface test** — A diagnostics or failover exercise can deliberately increment real counters. Match the exact `host` and `interface` to an approved change window before suppressing it.

2. **Virtual Ethernet lifecycle** — Container, bridge, bond, and virtual-machine interfaces can record small error or collision increments during expected reconfiguration. Confirm the interface type with `ip -details link` and suppress only the named ephemeral interface pattern for an expiring window.

3. **Counter discontinuity** — Reboot, device recreation, driver reload, namespace movement, or counter-width rollover can lower a cumulative value. The SPL sets that counter's delta to null and does not convert the lower value into new faults; use `counter_reset` and host boot/driver logs for diagnosis.

4. **Non-impacting isolated increment** — One genuine receive error may have no user-visible effect. Compare repeated five-minute deltas, packet loss, application latency, kernel messages, and switch-port counters before escalating severity; do not erase the observation from evidence.

**Safe suppression:** if local policy requires exceptions, append an owner-reviewed lookup keyed by both `host` and `interface`, with `start_time`, `end_time`, and `reason`. Expire every entry and retain unsuppressed raw results so a broad host exception cannot hide faults on unrelated adapters.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational Linux interface-health monitoring; no adversary behavior asserted)
reviewer: documentation review against Splunk and Linux kernel primary sources
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and counter semantics

Install the supported Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833) on the Linux Universal Forwarders that execute collection and on the search tier that provides the add-on's field extractions. Check the Splunkbase compatibility table against the deployed Splunk platform before rollout; this documentation review is not a claim that a particular platform/add-on pair ran in production. Follow the add-on's documented execution-permission and operating-system privilege requirements. Give operators read access to the chosen operating-system index without granting access to unrelated indexes.

The catalogue uses `os` as the index name. That is a local deployment choice and must be replaced consistently if the environment uses another index. The vendor-defined event source is the `interfaces.sh` scripted input with `sourcetype=interfaces`. Its extracted interface name and counters are `Name`, `RXerrors`, `TXerrors`, and `Collisions` with the capitalization shown.

Treat all three values as cumulative counters, not five-minute measurements. Linux exposes standard interface statistics through `struct rtnl_link_stats64`; `rx_errors` is the aggregate count of bad received packets, `tx_errors` is the aggregate count of transmit problems, and `collisions` counts transmit collisions. Standard counters persist across routine interface down/up operations, but reboot, device recreation, driver reload, namespace changes, rollover, or implementation-specific behavior can still create a decrease. A decrease is a discontinuity: the search emits a null delta for that counter rather than interpreting either the negative difference or the new absolute value as faults during the interval.

## 1. Enable and verify `interfaces.sh`

On a deployment copy of the add-on, locate the existing `interfaces.sh` stanza in `Splunk_TA_nix/default/inputs.conf` and copy only that stanza into `Splunk_TA_nix/local/inputs.conf`. Set `disabled=0`, route it to the selected event index, and use a 60-second interval. Preserve the script path, source, and `interfaces` sourcetype supplied by the installed add-on; do not create a substitute shell script or edit the `default` directory. Deploy the local override and restart the forwarder as required by the documented configuration-file workflow.

On one representative host, inspect the effective stanza with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` and confirm the local file wins. Then search `index=os sourcetype=interfaces earliest=-10m`. The collector runs once per host per interval and its table extraction should expose a row for each configured interface. Splunk documents that blank scripted-input columns can appear as `?`; the primary SPL uses `trim` and `tonumber`, so an unparseable field becomes null instead of participating in arithmetic.

Before saving an alert, run `index=os sourcetype=interfaces earliest=-10m | table _time host Name RXerrors TXerrors Collisions`. Confirm `Name` is populated and each available counter is numeric. On the same host compare a named adapter with `ip -s -s link show dev <interface>` and, where available, `/sys/class/net/<interface>/statistics/rx_errors`, `tx_errors`, and `collisions`. Values collected a minute apart can differ because the counters continue to advance; compare timestamps and direction of change, not merely copied screenshots.

## 2. Save and understand the delta search

Save the catalogue SPL as `linux_interface_error_increase_5m`. Run it every five minutes. Its inline bounds end at the current minute and read 15 minutes, providing at least two complete five-minute buckets when 60-second collection is healthy. `latest()` selects the chronologically newest counter in each bucket, and `_time+300<=now()` removes a bucket that is still open when a scheduled search starts late. `sort 0 host interface _time` is required before `streamstats`; `current=f window=1` then exposes the immediately preceding bucket for that same host and interface.

Each delta is calculated only when both adjacent values exist and the current value is not lower. The lower-value case remains null and sets `counter_reset=1`. `coalesce` treats unavailable individual deltas as zero only when summing the other valid fault increments. `eventstats max(_time)` and the `latest_bucket` filter prevent an older fault in the 15-minute lookback from being alerted again. The output retains current totals for diagnosis but alerts on `new_interface_faults`, never on the totals themselves.

The initial threshold, `new_interface_faults>=1`, means one newly counted receive error, transmit error, or collision during the latest five-minute aggregation window. It is deliberately sensitive and is not a percentage or per-second rate. Baseline physical, bonded, virtual, and container interfaces separately. If one increment is routine for a documented interface class, raise the count threshold through change control or add packet counters and calculate a true error ratio; do not label a raw count as an error rate.

The add-on maps `interfaces` to CIM Inventory. Inventory.Network can normalize interface identity, but it has no normalized receive-error, transmit-error, or collision counter. Do not create a `cimSpl` that substitutes the Performance.Network `thruput` field. This alert must use the raw add-on fields unless the organization owns and tests a custom data model.

## 3. Validate the detection logic

Perform the positive and negative control scenarios in this record with a temporary index and the same search-time extraction. Use fixed search bounds that include two adjacent complete buckets. The positive `eth0` sequence from 100 to 103 receive errors must produce one row with a delta of three. The unchanged `eth1` sequence must produce no row. The `eth2` sequence from 80 down to 2 must also produce no row; inspect the intermediate pipeline before the final `where` to verify `counter_reset=1` and a null receive delta.

Also inspect 24 hours of collection with `timechart span=5m count by host` to identify silent periods, and spot-check at least two physical interfaces against `ip -s -s link`. Record these as documentation and synthetic-search checks unless an authorized production test was actually performed. Do not change `status` to `verified` on the strength of this review.

## 4. Operationalize, respond, and preserve evidence

Trigger when result count is greater than zero and group work by `host` plus `interface`. Include the three deltas and current totals in the notification. Avoid a throttle that discards continuing increments; if the incident platform deduplicates, have it accumulate `new_interface_faults` while the issue remains open. A dashboard should show a latest-fault table, three separately labelled delta trends, and drilldowns to kernel messages, host boot events, and deployment or maintenance changes.

The runbook should first rerun `ip -s -s link show dev <interface>` and determine whether the counter is still increasing. Use `ethtool -S <interface>` for driver-specific detail, then inspect `journalctl -k` for link, driver, reset, and firmware messages. For a physical adapter, compare the connected switch port, optics/cable, speed, and duplex. For a bond, bridge, virtual Ethernet pair, or container interface, identify the owning workload before changing it. RX/TX errors do not include every dropped-packet condition, so use a separate drop-counter search when loss is suspected.

Retain the saved-search definition, scheduler history, alert results, and dashboard export under the operations evidence policy. If an exception lookup is added locally, preserve its owner, exact host/interface key, reason, and expiry alongside the evidence.

## 5. Troubleshoot source and search failures

No `interfaces` events usually means the supplied stanza is still disabled, the add-on is absent from the forwarder, the script lacks execute permission, or routing uses another index. Events with no extracted fields usually mean the search-tier copy of `Splunk_TA_nix` is absent, the sourcetype was changed, or incomplete event processing broke the table extraction. A field containing `?` is a documented blank value; determine why the host command omitted it rather than converting it to zero.

A first sample for a new interface has no previous value and must not alert. If it does, confirm the search still uses `current=f window=1` and is sorted by `host interface _time`. Repeated alerts on an old nonzero total indicate someone replaced the delta logic with an absolute-value test. Missing high-cardinality results can indicate an unintended `sort` limit; retain `sort 0` after controlling the search scope. If Splunk differs from the host, compare collection timestamps, verify the exact case-sensitive fields, and check whether the device was recreated between samples before blaming arithmetic.
grandmaExplanation: We watch each Linux server's network adapters for newly reported send, receive, or collision problems. That helps the team investigate a faulty link or adapter before intermittent trouble becomes an outage.
